# Phase 2: Muscle-memory implementations

*from week 5, repeated weekly* · [Track on the site](https://arubad.github.io/AI_Research_Journey/#p2)

This is the HAND list: the boilerplate core you must reproduce from a blank file, with every AI tool off, under the time target. Alisa's rule, which the CS336 honor code also enforces: practice with AI assistance completely off, because you will underestimate your reliance otherwise. Rotate through the table once a week until every row is under target three times in a row; after that, one timed row per day keeps it warm.

| # | Implementation | Time target | Must get right | Drilled in | Folder |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Scaled dot-product attention | 10 min | The √d_k scaling, −∞ (not 0) in the causal mask, softmax over the key axis | #4 Transformer | `01-sdpa/` |
| 2 | Multi-head attention | 20 min | Split heads → attend → merge via reshape or `einsum`; output projection W_O | #4 Transformer | `02-multi-head-attention/` |
| 3 | Full pre-norm decoder block | 30 min | LN → MHA → residual → LN → FFN (4×d_model, GeLU or SwiGLU) → residual; parameter count by hand | #4, #16 LLaMA | `03-decoder-block/` |
| 4 | BPE tokenizer | 45 min | Build vocab from a corpus; encode a new string; state the merge-step complexity | CS336 A1, Phase 4 | `04-bpe-tokenizer/` |
| 5 | Top-k / top-p sampling with temperature | 15 min | Temperature before filtering; masking that keeps at least one token | CS336 L10 | `05-sampling/` |
| 6 | Beam search | 20 min | Track log-probs across B beams; handle EOS and length normalization | CS336 L10 | `06-beam-search/` |
| 7 | Full training loop | 20 min | Forward, loss, `backward()`, optimizer step, scheduler step, grad clipping, eval split | #2 Adam, #6 GPT-3 | `07-training-loop/` |
| 8 | NumPy backprop | 45 min | Linear → softmax → cross-entropy, analytic gradients, no autograd | #1 AlexNet, Phase 1 | `08-numpy-backprop/` |
| 9 | Adam optimizer | 15 min | m, v, bias correction, decoupled weight decay | #2 Adam | `09-adam/` |
| 10 | LoRA wrapper around `nn.Linear` | 10 min | B = 0 init, A ~ N(0, σ²), α/r scaling, merge for inference | #10 LoRA | `10-lora/` |
| 11 | RoPE | 15 min | Complex rotation of Q and K; dot product depends only on m − n | #16 LLaMA | `11-rope/` |
| 12 | KV cache for generation | 20 min | Prefill vs decode; append K, V per step; compute only the new Q | CS336 L10 | `12-kv-cache/` |
| 13 | GQA / MQA attention | 15 min | n_kv_heads < n_heads via `repeat_interleave`; KV-cache memory drops by n_heads/n_kv_heads | #16 LLaMA | `13-gqa/` |
| 14 | DPO loss | 10 min | `-logsigmoid(β((πw−refw)−(πl−refl))).mean()` | #13 DPO | `14-dpo-loss/` |
| 15 | GRPO advantage + clipped loss | 20 min | Group-normalized advantages, importance ratio with stop-gradient on old log-probs, clip | #19 GRPO | `15-grpo-loss/` |
| 16 | PPO clipped surrogate + GAE | 30 min | `min(rA, clip(r,1−ε,1+ε)A)`, GAE recursion, value loss, entropy bonus | #8 PPO | `16-ppo-loss/` |
| 17 | Online (tiled) softmax | 20 min | Running max and denominator rescaled by exp(m_old − m_new); `allclose` vs `F.softmax` | #17 FlashAttention | `17-online-softmax/` |
| 18 | Top-k MoE router | 20 min | Softmax gate, top-2 dispatch, load-balancing auxiliary loss | #18 MoE | `18-moe-router/` |
| 19 | Flow-matching loss + Euler sampler | 15 min | x_t = (1−t)x₀ + t x₁, v_θ ≈ x₁ − x₀, Euler loop | #21 Flow Matching | `19-flow-matching/` |

**Reference implementations to read once, then close.** Karpathy's [build-nanogpt](https://github.com/karpathy/build-nanogpt) and [minbpe](https://github.com/karpathy/minbpe) ([Neural Networks: Zero to Hero playlist](https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLAqhIrjkxbuWI23v9cThsA9GvCAUhRvKZ)), [The Illustrated GPT-2](https://jalammar.github.io/illustrated-gpt2/), and the [CS224N self-attention and Transformers notes](https://web.stanford.edu/class/cs224n/readings/cs224n-self-attention-transformers-2023_draft.pdf). Read them before the first drill, never during one.

**AGENT work around the drills.** Have a coding agent build you a drill harness: a repo with one `test_<row>.py` per row that asserts your from-scratch output against the PyTorch reference, plus a timer. You write the implementation files; the agent writes and maintains the tests.

[Neural Networks: Zero to Hero playlist](https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLAqhIrjkxbuWI23v9cThsA9GvCAUhRvKZ)

## How to run a drill
1. AI tools and autocomplete off. Start a timer.
2. Write the implementation from a blank file in `NN-name/attempts/YYYY-MM-DD.py`.
3. Run `pytest tests/test_NN.py` (the agent-built harness checks it against the PyTorch reference).
4. Log it in `drill_log.csv` and on the site (Under target / Missed). Three under target in a row clears the row.
